covers: Monday 2 November 2026, JSE session to the US afternoon (to 22:10 SAST)
headline: Breaking: US to remove South Africa from AGOA from 1 January 2027; oil down about 8% on Iran peace-talk hopes as Nasdaq and S&P 500 turn negative
summary: The US Trade Representative said on Monday that South Africa and Rwanda will lose duty-free access under AGOA from 1 January 2027; AGOA preferential exports were about $1.7 billion, roughly 10% of SA's shipments to the US (USTR via eNCA and SA People, 2 Nov). On Wall Street, early gains faded: by 14:34 New York time (21:34 SAST) the S&P 500 was down 0.1% at 7,572.54 and the Nasdaq down 0.4% at 25,329.99, while the Dow was up 0.7% at 52,115.90 as money rotated from tech into staples, utilities and health care (Investing.com, 2 Nov). Brent fell 7.6% to $104.81 and the US 10-year yield eased to about 4.90% on Iran peace-talk hopes (Investing.com, 2 Nov) — Apple and Palantir results after 23:00 SAST and Tuesday's US midterms are the next tests.

items.title: US to remove South Africa from AGOA duty-free trade from 1 January 2027
items.summary: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on 2 November that South Africa and Rwanda engage in practices 'inconsistent' with AGOA's eligibility rules, citing barriers to US trade and investment and foreign-policy and security concerns. Removal needs 60 days' notice, and SA People reports it takes effect on 1 January 2027. AGOA preferential exports were about $1.7 billion (about R28 billion), roughly 10% of SA's shipments to the US; about 89% of SA exports to the US already enter on standard WTO terms, and vehicles and steel already face separate 25% and 50% US tariffs (SA People, 2 Nov). Trade Minister Parks Tau has said the economy will remain stable as SA seeks other markets (eNCA, 2 Nov).

items.title: Oil falls about 8% (Brent $104.81) as Iran signals openness to peace talks
items.summary: Brent crude was down 7.6% at $104.81 a barrel in the US afternoon on 2 November, after reports that the US is giving diplomacy with Iran more room before any renewed military action (Investing.com, 2 Nov, 14:34 New York time). Earlier in the day Brent was down 6.3% at $106.2 and WTI 6.4% at $97.4 (TradingKey, 2 Nov). Lower oil helps the rand and SA fuel-price outlook, but hurts oil producers.

items.title: Marvell agrees to buy Lumentum (LRC scanner BUY) for about $115 billion in shares; Lumentum falls about 11%
items.summary: Marvell will pay a fixed 4.5 Marvell shares for each Lumentum share, valuing Lumentum at about $115 billion (enterprise value), or roughly $1,132 a share, a 23.9% premium to Lumentum's unaffected 28 October close. Marvell holders would own about 67% of the combined company; closing is expected in the first half of 2028, subject to shareholder and regulatory approval (Marvell press release, 2 Nov 2026). In Monday trading Lumentum was quoted at $745.10 (−11.4%) and Marvell at $183.63 (−6.5%) (Investing.com quotes, 2 Nov 2026), versus Friday closes of $840.70 and $196.40 (LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026). Lumentum is rated BUY and Marvell HOLD by the LRC Stock Scanner; this brief does not change ratings. Lumentum's own results were due on 5 November.
items.source: Marvell press release, 2 Nov 2026; Investing.com, 2 Nov 2026; LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026

items.title: Iran: a 'two-day plan' brokered by Qatar and Pakistan could reopen the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Speaking to Al Jazeera on Sunday, Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said Qatari and Pakistani mediators had reworked Iran's original seven-day plan and 'we have now reached a two-day plan': on day one 'America will implement a set of measures' and on day two the strait would reopen. The measures were not specified; security chief Mohsen Rezaei said the blockade would stay until conditions including 'releasing frozen assets' were met, and said the tone of a letter from US Vice President JD Vance had 'completely changed'. Trump said on Saturday the talks were 'going fine but you know they're not very reliable' (Arab News, 2 Nov 2026). This is the main driver behind Monday's oil fall; nothing has been agreed yet.

items.title: Nasdaq and S&P 500 give up early gains and turn negative as money rotates out of tech; Dow up 0.7%
items.summary: At 14:34 New York time (21:34 SAST) the S&P 500 was down 0.1% at 7,572.54 after rising as much as 1.1%, and the Nasdaq was down 0.4% at 25,329.99 after being up as much as 1.4%; the Dow was up 0.7% at 52,115.90. AI shares fell again, weighed by Oracle's planned $20 billion stock-and-bond raise, while consumer staples, utilities and health care gained. The US 10-year Treasury yield was about 4.90% (Investing.com, 2 Nov).

items.title: US factories beat forecasts: ISM manufacturing 55.5 in October, price pressure eases a little
items.summary: The ISM manufacturing PMI rose to 55.5 in October from 54.5 in September (ISM, 2 Nov 2026), above the 54.7 expected (Yahoo Finance, 2 Nov 2026). Production rose to 59.0 from 56.7 and new orders to 55.5 from 55.3, while employment eased to 52.4 from 52.7. The prices index fell to 75.2 from 77.9 but remains very high (ISM, 2 Nov 2026). Strong activity with high prices keeps the Fed's next move in focus ahead of Friday's jobs report.
items.source: ISM via PR Newswire, 2 Nov 2026; Yahoo Finance, 2 Nov 2026

items.title: Oracle files to raise $20 billion in stock and bonds for its AI build-out; shares lower
items.summary: Oracle filed on Monday to raise $20 billion — $10 billion through a common-stock sale and $10 billion in senior notes — for general corporate purposes including capital spending and debt repayment. The shares fell 3% before the open (Dataconomy, 2 Nov 2026) and were quoted at $123.27 (−5.7%) in Monday trading (Investing.com, 2 Nov 2026), against a Friday close of $130.70. Oracle shares are down about 33% in 2026 on worries about the debt needed to fund AI infrastructure (Dataconomy). Oracle is rated HOLD by the LRC Stock Scanner.
items.source: Dataconomy, 2 Nov 2026; Investing.com, 2 Nov 2026; LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026

items.title: Busy week: midterms Tuesday, October jobs report Friday, and Apple, Palantir, AMD and Qualcomm results
items.summary: Apple and Palantir report after the US close on Monday 2 November; AMD reports after the close on Tuesday 3 November, Qualcomm and Arm on Wednesday 4 November. ISM services is due on Wednesday. The US midterm elections are on Tuesday 3 November, and the October employment report comes on Friday 6 November at 8:30 ET (15:30 SAST, now that US clocks have moved back). The Fed's target range is 3.75%–4.00% (TradingKey, 2 Nov 2026). Reuters reported about an 80% chance of a December Fed hike (Tech Insider, Nov 2026).

items.title: Rand firmer at R16.64 and JSE Top 40 up about 1% as oil slides
items.summary: At 12:48 GMT (14:48 SAST) on Monday 2 November the rand traded at R16.64 per dollar, about 0.4% firmer than Friday's close, after the Absa PMI improved; the JSE Top 40 was up about 1% and the yield on the 2035 government bond fell 2.5 basis points to 8.565% (Reuters via CNBC Africa, 2 Nov 2026).

items.title: Absa PMI improves to 49.6 in October, a second monthly gain, but factories are still contracting
items.summary: The seasonally adjusted Absa manufacturing PMI rose 0.9 points to 49.6 in October from a revised 48.7 in September, just below the 50-point line. All five headline components improved: business activity 48.6 (from 47.7), new sales orders 46.8 (45.4), employment 44.2 (42.8), inventories 50.4 (49.7) and supplier deliveries 58.1 (58.0). But the purchasing price index climbed to 73.7 from 71.1 and expected business conditions in six months fell to 51.7 from 55.3; the report said demand 'remains insufficient to support a sustained recovery' and 'the recovery remains fragile' (Absa PMI via IT-Online, 2 Nov 2026; Reuters via Club of Mozambique, 2 Nov 2026). Rising input costs are a watch point for SA inflation and the SARB.
items.source: IT-Online, 2 Nov 2026; Reuters via Club of Mozambique, 2 Nov 2026

items.title: Aspen sells European rights to women's health product Ovestin for €197 million
items.summary: Aspen Pharmacare agreed on 2 November to sell the European commercialisation rights and related intellectual property for Ovestin to Ennogen Healthcare International for €197 million (about $220 million), plus about €4 million for inventory. Aspen said the money goes to its capital allocation plans, with share buybacks its preferred way to return capital (CNBC Africa / Reuters, 2 Nov).

items.title: Wednesday 4 November is a public holiday for the local government elections
items.summary: President Cyril Ramaphosa declared local government election day, 4 November, a public holiday under the Public Holidays Act by notice in the Government Gazette (BusinessTech). That makes this a four-day trading week for South Africa, with US results and the midterm outcome landing around the holiday.

items.title: Concor, the PIC-owned construction group, is in business rescue; more than 2,200 jobs at risk
items.summary: Concor's board found the business financially distressed and filed for business rescue on 6 October 2026, covering Concor Holdings, Concor (Pty) Ltd, Concor Construction and Concor Mining. The company is owned by the GEPF (81.25%) and UIF (18.75%), managed by the PIC, which cites liquidity and working-capital strain, legacy projects and guarantee calls after partner Murray & Roberts' 2024 rescue. Moneyweb reports more than 2,200 jobs at risk; Concor is a joint-venture partner on the R1.65 billion Msikaba bridge on the N2 Wild Coast road (Moneyweb, 2 Nov 2026).

items.title: Gold back near $3,900 after its worst October since 2008; platinum still falling
items.summary: At 01:01 GMT on Monday spot gold was up 0.6% at $3,900.05 an ounce and silver up 1.4% at $49.83, while platinum was down 3.4% at $1,434.65 and palladium down 2.6% at $980.35. Gold had fallen 3.7% to a one-year low in the prior session. Lower oil eased some inflation worries; the US dollar index was down 0.2% at 101.88 (Investing.com, 2 Nov 2026).

items.title: Goldman Sachs lifts its December Brent forecast to $105 from $90
items.summary: Goldman raised its December forecasts to $105 for Brent (from $90) and $94 for WTI, and its 2027 averages to $88 for Brent (from $80) and $78 for WTI (from $73), citing supply risks from the Middle East and Russia–Ukraine and adding a 1 million barrel-a-day disruption allowance to its 2027 base case (investingLive, 2 Nov 2026).

items.title: Apple and Palantir report after the US close tonight (after 23:00 SAST); both HOLD
items.summary: Apple (HOLD, score 61) and Palantir (HOLD, score 72) closed Friday at $344.63 and $184.11 (LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026). For Apple's September quarter, analysts expect earnings of about $2.00 a share on revenue of about $113.46 billion; it is new CEO John Ternus's first results (Yahoo Finance, 2 Nov 2026). Apple was about 1% lower in Monday trading (Investing.com, 2 Nov 2026). Results can move the scanner score; this brief does not change ratings.
items.source: LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026; Yahoo Finance, 2 Nov 2026; Investing.com, 2 Nov 2026

items.title: AMD (Tuesday) and QCOM (Wednesday) report after Friday's chip sell-off
items.summary: AMD (HOLD, score 69) fell 10.9% to $504.80 on Friday and Qualcomm (HOLD, score 39) 11.1% to $164.79 in the Intel-led chip sell-off (LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026). AMD reports after the close on Tuesday 3 November and Qualcomm on Wednesday 4 November (TradingKey, 2 Nov 2026).
items.source: LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026; TradingKey, 2 Nov 2026

items.title: JSE gold and PGM miners closed Friday 5.6–6.4% lower; gold's Monday bounce is a first test
items.summary: On Friday 30 October Gold Fields fell 6.4% to R553.06, Sibanye-Stillwater 6.4% to R35.77, Harmony 6.3% to R245.58, AngloGold Ashanti 6.0% to R1,340.52 and Implats 5.6% to R163.91, while Sasol rose 1.2% to R289.45 on higher oil (LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026). Spot gold's 0.6% rise in Asia (Investing.com, 2 Nov) is the first sign for Monday's open; platinum is still down.
items.source: LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026; Investing.com, 2 Nov 2026
